title: Runner
leads: Nobody. You look after every phone in your bag, from one signature to the next.
where: On the road between three hub sites in one area and their hub
hours: Evenings and nights. From the end of the site's shift to 10:00 PM, then the return before 7:00 AM
summary: You carry three sites' phones to the hub every night and bring them back before 7:00 AM, signed for at both ends.

posting.headline: Runner (night logistics), Cairo
posting.about: KMSC runs the field operations behind one of the most ambitious artificial intelligence projects in the region, at factories, warehouses, and farms across Cairo. Every night the kit from three sites goes to a hub and comes back before the morning shift. A runner makes that trip by vehicle, with every device counted and signed for at both ends.
do: Count the site's devices with the Portfolio Manager or the site lead, and both of you sign the list.
Take all of a site's kit in one trip, in the provided bag.
Drive straight to your hub with no stops, and make your last drop of the night before 10:00 PM.
Count again with the hub attendant and sign, then do the same at your next site.
In the morning, bring the kit back to the same three sites and sign it over before 7:00 AM.
At a checkpoint, show the company letter and the signed list, stay calm, and call your manager, the Planning and Logistics Lead.
need: A national ID, a valid driving licence, and a vehicle.
Careful with equipment and honest with numbers.
Calm with people, even at a checkpoint, and never one to argue.
plus: You have worked as a driver or a courier before.
You know your side of Cairo at night.
offer: A steady monthly wage, paid on time.
Paid training, with your trainer next to you on your first run.
A clear job with a clear list, in a company that writes everything down.
The company letter and two numbers that always answer, so you are never alone on the road.
posting.apply: Send your name, your age, your area, your phone number, and whether you have a driving licence and a vehicle. We call you back within two working days to book your onboarding screening.

offer.heading: Offer of employment
paragraphs: We are pleased to offer you the position of Runner at KMSC. You will report to {manager}, the Planning and Logistics Lead.
Your start date is {start}. You start with one hour of paid training, then your first run with your trainer.

terms.label: Place of work
terms.v: Three hub sites in one area and their hub. Home hub: {site}.

terms.label: Hours
terms.v: Evenings and nights, at the hub by 10:00 PM and back before 7:00 AM

terms.label: Pay
terms.v: {pay} per month, paid at the end of the month

conditions: A copy of your national ID and your driving licence.
Your signature on the consent form and the fraud briefing.
One account in your own name. Accounts are never shared.
The one-hour training and your first run, signed off by your trainer.
expect: Every run is at the hub before 10:00 PM, or it does not leave.
Every phone you sign for at one end is signed in at the other.
You never stop on the way. A phone that goes home with you ends the job.
offer.closing: Please sign below to accept this offer. We look forward to working with you.

handbook.purpose: The client pays only for footage that reaches them. A full phone that sleeps at the site is a lost day. You carry three sites' phones to the hub every night and bring them back empty before the operators clock in. Every handover is counted and signed.
outcomes: Every site's phones at the hub before 10:00 PM, every night.
Every cleared phone back at its site, signed for, before 7:00 AM.
Two signatures on the phone list at every handover.
The Planning and Logistics Lead hears about a problem from the road, not the next morning.
daily: Evening. Tonight's plan from the Planning and Logistics Lead: your three sites and your hub. Check the letter kit.
Pickup. Count by device number against the phone list. Both sign. Bag closed, bag on you.
On the road. Straight to the hub. No fuel, no food, no passenger, no errand.
At the hub. Count with the hub attendant. Both sign.
Next site. Same again, one bag per site. Last drop before 10:00 PM.
Early morning. Collect the cleared phones. New list, both sign. Held phones stay.
Before 7:00 AM. The same three sites as last night. Hand the bag to the operator. Count together. Both sign.
By 8:00 PM the night before. Tell the Planning and Logistics Lead about any absence. A spare takes your run.
weekly: Thursday night. The full flush: every phone from every site goes to the hub.
Once a week. Check the bag, the letter kit, and the vehicle. Replace what is worn.
monthly: Go through the month's runs with the Planning and Logistics Lead. Agree on what to change.
standards: One runner, three sites, one area, one vehicle. The morning return is the same runner and the same three sites.
One bag per site, all of its phones, nothing on the outside.
The phone list is in the bag, signed by both sides at pickup and at drop.
The letter kit rides on every run. No letter, no run.
MDM tracking is on while the phones travel.
Sign only the real count. A wrong number is a call to the Planning and Logistics Lead.
Missing at the end of a shift with no word: a spare is called before 6:00 PM, and your run is theirs tonight.
never: A run that cannot reach the hub by 10:00 PM does not leave.
Never stop on the way, for anything.
A phone that goes home with you ends the job.
Never argue with the police, and never hide the count.
Saying the client's name to anyone outside the company ends the job.

firstMonth.what: One hour with the Planning and Logistics Lead: the bag, the list, the letter kit, the checkpoint answer.
Your trainer rides with you. You do every count and every signature yourself.
You run your three sites alone. The Planning and Logistics Lead checks your signed lists every morning.
You pass the quiz, know the checkpoint answer by heart, and every run is on time.

measures: Runs at the hub before 10:00 PM, every night.
Phones back at the site, signed, before 7:00 AM.
Two signatures at every handover. No gaps.
Counts that did not match, per month.
handbook.call: The Planning and Logistics Lead, for everything on the run, at any hour. A late run, a wrong count, the police, a crash, a theft: call now. Then Moharam. If the police keep a phone, Mano brings a lawyer the same day.
